One defect caught by the released analysis: the kernel's in-flight summary counted a phantom accepted step per lineage because the ledger logs scores at 12 dp and an echo row's rounded score sits 5e-13 above the unrounded seed constant; exact recomputation and all 33 kernel state files agree the true count is zero everywhere.

arms.label: Wave 4 — capability-tier control (DISSOCIATION)
arms.design: The strongest alternative reading of §3 — that echo is what any sufficiently weak proposer does — was left standing by every ladder because no experiment varied capability with precision out of the design. Registered in wave4_prereg_tiers_heilbronn.md (SHA-256 7b3e67dc…, published to an externally-timestamped host before any row was sampled): three hosted capability tiers, requested by explicit model parameter, running the identical Heilbronn n = 13 lineage protocol — same seed parent extracted programmatically from the wave-3 runner rather than retyped, same echo definition, tools forbidden and tool_uses recorded per row.
arms.result: 0 of 120 coordinate-verified echoes — every tier at 0% against a registered ≤ 30% bound — verdict DISSOCIATION, printed by the analysis script itself, which recomputes every echo and score from stored coordinates. The registered secondary (5.2, echo monotonicity) returned NOT EVALUATED, its 10-echo floor unmet. The failures differ in kind rather than degree: no proposal in any tier improved on the seed (0/120), and the registered template check finds valid outputs scoring exactly zero — three-plus collinear points — at 52.5% for the weakest tier, 27.5% for the middle and 97.5% for the strongest, whose 39/40 zero-scoring outputs are family-similar symmetric lattices, pairwise distinct at 6 dp.
arms.verdict: held — capability does not reproduce the quantization ladder's failure mode
arms.caveats: 0/120 bounds echo at roughly 3% at this n, not an exclusion at any rate, and the dissociation bounds the capability confound over the tiers sampled without excluding it below them. Scope limits are the prereg's own: served precision, sampling parameters and serving path per tier are all unattested (C3); one date; one harness wrapper. On LABS, a third task where nothing climbed, the same rungs' stall-echo rates reversed, so the stuck-tier contrast is Heilbronn-specific rather than a law of stalls. The all-distinct uniqueness count is post-hoc and not computed by the replay script.

arms.label: Wave 5 — LABS discrete-task transfer
arms.design: Registered in wave5_prereg_labs.md (SHA a1336cfd…, runner SHA d1739f6c…, pushed as a public Kaggle kernel before sampling): low-autocorrelation binary sequences at n = 32, a discrete task with no float arithmetic, registered specifically to test the 'echo is float-rounding' reading. 495 calls on the same 14B GGUF ladder. Its §8b predicted its own failure mode before running.
arms.result: The Q4_K_M rung accepted zero steps, the control floor fired, verdict UNINFORMATIVE (Branch C), and no branch of its decision rule is claimed. Its unclaimable descriptives run in the opposite direction from every other wave: echo 10/233 = 4.3% at Q2_K against 12/60 = 20.0% at Q4_K_M — reversed, on a task where a single flipped symbol is a complete departure — with 0 improving departures anywhere and 0 symmetry variants.
arms.verdict: not evaluable — UNINFORMATIVE by its own registered floor
arms.caveats: Reported rather than shelved. Two of the three transfer tasks designed were too hard for the model that had to climb them, which is a fact about task calibration and is disclosed as such. The reversal is what makes wave 4's stuck-tier contrast Heilbronn-specific rather than a general law about stalls.

arms.label: Wave 7 — family generality (Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B)
arms.design: Every GGUF figure comes from a single model family, so wave7_prereg_families.md (SHA-256 44244005…, published as a public Kaggle dataset before sampling) registered the same circle-packing protocol, byte-identical prompts and evaluator on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-it — per-family directional contrasts only, no absolute band imported from any prior task or family, echo primary not floor-gated, a 20-valid-row power floor per rung, and a disconfirmation clause committing the authors to qualify §3's claims as Qwen-specific if the contrast was refuted in both families.
arms.result: Neither family reached its power floor; wave7_analysis.py prints UNDERPOWERED for both, the control floors also fire, and the disconfirmation clause — which requires both families evaluable and refuted — does not. Llama produced 1 valid packing in 50 at Q4_K_M and 5 in 50 at Q2_K, failing by the same wrong-count lottery the 7B Qwen ladder shows (counts scattered 18–30 around the demanded 26); Gemma produced 14 and 4 — and, as an unclaimable descriptive, all 18 of Gemma's valid outputs at both rungs are coordinate-exact parent echoes, while none of Llama's 6 are.
arms.verdict: not evaluable — UNDERPOWERED in both arms; establishes a scope fact, not a transfer fact
arms.caveats: The 8–9B open-weight class sits below this task's competence floor at every precision tested. One defect in the locked, public and immutable registration is disclosed: its informational prior-state section quotes Qwen echo figures from working notes ('94% / 60% / 51% against 15% / 10% / 24%') where ledger replay gives 94%/15% for the registered wave, 79% (19/24) against 6% (1/17) for the fresh wave and 75% against 43% for the IQ2 pair; the discrepancy sits in a priors section, not in any registered bound, floor or verdict.

arms.label: Wave 7b — competence-matched retry (Phi-4, Mistral-Small-24B)
arms.design: A competence-matched retry registered in wave7b_prereg_families_14b.md (SHA-256 cd043d63…, public Kaggle dataset pushed before sampling), re-running the identical protocol on Phi-4 (14.7B) and Mistral-Small-24B — the same size class as, and larger than, the Qwen model where the cliff lives — with the same 20-valid-row power floor and a registered both-underpowered branch written for exactly this outcome.
arms.result: Both arms again miss the floor: Phi-4 produced 9 valid packings in 100 loop calls (6/50 Q2_K, 3/50 Q4_K_M), Mistral 2 (1/50 and 1/50). The registered both-underpowered branch holds, so the task's format-competence floor excluded every non-Qwen family tested at up to 24B, and the family-generality limitation is stated as unresolved in the abstract's scope sentence as that branch requires. Unclaimable descriptives: unlike the 8–9B arms these climbed — four of Phi-4's five Q2_K lineages improved past the seed (best 1.30, one Q4_K_M lineage reaching 2.1667), Mistral improved in one lineage per rung with a Q2_K best of 2.1667 — and neither model echoed even once at either rung.
arms.verdict: not evaluable — UNDERPOWERED in both arms; the registered both-underpowered branch fires
arms.caveats: Across all four non-Qwen arms the 35 valid outputs split into Gemma's 18 (every one a parent echo, at both rungs) and the other three families' 17 (not one echo), so whatever governs parent-copying is not bit-width alone — on these small samples it looks family-shaped, which is what the registered FAMILY-DEPENDENT reporting rule anticipated and what remains untested at adequate power. Phi-4's must-differ probe returned the instruction-sensitive branch vacuously: that branch exists to explain loop echo and Phi-4 produced none. A family ladder needs either a coder-tuned non-Qwen 14B that can hold the output format or a format-forgiving task; both are named as open work.

arms.label: Wave 7c — screen-selected sixth family (gemma-4-31b) clears the control floor
arms.design: Registered in wave7c_prereg_screened_families.md (SHA-256 b1fc9ee9…, public Kaggle dataset pushed before sampling); changes the selection procedure, not the test. A disclosed competence screen — 50 one-shot generation-0 calls per model through OpenRouter free-tier aliases, instrument committed before screen sampling — gates a local pinned-weight ladder: a pass gates, a fail gates nothing, and no screen number is evidence, since the screen's serving path is unattested. Five candidates screened: gemma-4-31b-it 43/50 valid, nemotron-3-super 34/50 (ADVANCE but exceeds free-tier hardware, advanced-not-run), gpt-oss-20b 27/50 ADVANCE; nemotron-nano and north-mini-code below the ≥ 20/50 bar, the latter with 49 of 50 rows reasoning-censored empties. Three registered outcomes on the ladder: 7c.1 echo primary (20-valid floor per rung), 7c.2 floor-gated search-progress secondary (Q4_K_M control floor ≥ 1.0 accepted steps), 7c.3 must-differ probe at Q2_K.
arms.result: gemma-4-31b returned the wave's only informative verdicts. 7c.2 HELD: the Q4_K_M control floor passed — the first non-Qwen arm in the programme to clear one, mean accepted steps 4.800 against the ≥ 1.0 floor, all five seeds improving, best 2.08 on every seed — and Q2_K takes 0.000 accepted steps against 4.800, reproducing the 2-bit search-activity collapse under a registered floor-gated prediction. 7c.1 UNDERPOWERED: 0 valid Q2_K packings in 50 against the 20-valid floor (Q4_K_M: 24), no branch claimed. 7c.3 UNDERPOWERED: 0 of 10 probes valid at Q2_K (Q4_K_M 10/10 valid, 0 echoes-under-differ). The collapse channel differs from every family before it: at Q2_K gemma-4 stays viable — 48 of 50 calls parseable, identical to Q4_K_M — while producing nothing valid and echoing nothing (Q4_K_M echo 0/24). Well-formed invalidity is a third failure channel, equally invisible to viability-style health metrics, where Qwen's is parent-copying and gemma-2's 18 valid outputs were all echoes. gpt-oss-20b's ladder returned UNDERPOWERED: 5/50 valid at Q4_K_M — every one a coordinate-exact parent echo — and 0/50 at Q2_K.
arms.verdict: 7c.2 HELD — one directional replication of the search-activity collapse, not a resolved generalization; 7c.1 and 7c.3 UNDERPOWERED, so the echo-contrast primary remains unresolved beyond Qwen
arms.caveats: The gemma retry required a post-registration runner edit with no pre-resumption amendment — unlike every arm-level serving-path deviation in the corpus — so the commit-pair diff (8cfaffb → 342cdea, 18 lines confined to the model-download path; seeds, prompts, sampling parameters and sampling code unchanged) stands as an after-the-fact substitute, a named gap in amendment discipline. Rungs are community GGUF conversions (gpt-oss additionally MXFP4-native, qualifier registered before the run), so 2-bit precision versus conversion quality is not disentangled. The channel taxonomy is descriptive and unregistered, like every cross-family comparison in the section; the screen ledger logged one unchanged alias served by four different providers within a single 50-call run — the serving heterogeneity §5 argues an alias leaves unattested, observed live.

stats.7c2: HELD: 0.000 vs 4.800 accepted steps, floor passed, all 5 seeds improved

arms.label: Wave-8 pilot — seed calibration against wave 3's control-rung floor
arms.design: A disclosed seed-calibration pilot (kaggle_wave8_pilot/, public kernel sohamgugalet/wave8-seed-pilot, Q4_K_M only, no Q2_K rows) testing whether an easier seed would repair wave 3's fired control-arm floor. Four graded best-of-K random parents, scores 0.000308 to 0.003544, against wave 3's registered seed at 0.009087.
arms.result: The control rung improved on 1 of 40 probes — even from a best-of-1 random configuration — and echoed 6 of 8 valid outputs at the easiest seed. The floor is the task, not the seed: no seed choice makes Heilbronn a search-progress instrument for this model, so the search-progress hypotheses stay tested on circle packing alone and the recalibrated wave the pilot was scoped for is not run. The pilot also shows, on 40 disclosed unregistered rows, that the reference rung's regression toward copying on this task (46.9%) is not an artifact of the registered seed's difficulty.
arms.verdict: descriptive — the conditional question wave 3 could not answer stays open
arms.caveats: 40 unregistered rows, Q4_K_M only, no Q2_K arm, so nothing about the rung contrast can be drawn from it directly.

arms.label: Item-4 self-audit — the duration-CV canary fires on a fixed serving path
arms.design: Item 4 is the one element of the disclosure standard the paper claims as new, so it is audited against the paper's own rows: §3's ledgers carry per-invocation wall_s across weight files pinned by SHA-256 on a fixed inference stack — same llama.cpp build, a single Tesla P100, same sampling parameters, same harness. Whatever the canary reports there, it is not reporting a serving-path change, because there was none. Released as sec6_cv_canary_audit.py.
arms.result: It fires. Duration CV among valid rows is 0.0603 at Q4_K_M and 0.0143 at Q2_K — a ratio of 0.237, below the one-third threshold the item names — with wave 2 replicating on independent seeds at 0.0692 against 0.0200 (ratio 0.289) and a permutation test returning p < 0.0001 on both. Q3_K_M does not fire on either wave (ratios 0.949 and 1.066), so the canary is selectively wrong at exactly the rung §3 is about. The mechanism is output degeneracy, not serving: duration CV is low among echo rows at every rung (0.0210, 0.0141, 0.0113) and high among non-echo rows at every rung (0.0783, 0.0778, 0.0294). The obvious repair — throughput over non-echo valid rows only — fails three ways: wave 1's ranges are not disjoint (Q4_K_M's [16.455, 18.188] entirely contains Q2_K's [16.703, 16.753]); a ~92% cold-start effect uniform across all twelve rung × wave cells silently did the filtering; and the band does not survive a hardware change, with the same SHA-pinned files inverting order between a P100 (Q4_K_M 17.94 vs Q2_K 16.62 tok/s) and 2 × T4 (21.45 vs 22.48).
arms.verdict: disconfirmed — item 4's firing condition is withdrawn in its dispersion form and not replaced
arms.caveats: The disclosure half is retained because it costs nothing and enables exactly this audit. This does not overturn §4, whose serving-signature evidence is an absolute latency gap of one to two orders rather than a dispersion ratio and whose arm was not echoing at all. It does not show that no observable attests the served file — output-side methods exist — only that the one instrument class a verifier can compute from what an agent runtime already returns is ruled out, for a reason that worsens when the verifier loses the hardware.

arms.label: Scope conditions — family generality and serving-path non-identifiability
arms.design: The two limitations the paper states as unresolved rather than estimated: whether the cliff is a Qwen-family artifact, and whether any observable can attest which serving path answered a past call. The first was attacked by two registered family waves and a competence-matched retry; the second by the two runnable within-runtime experiments and an engagement with output-text fingerprinting.
arms.result: Family generality is unresolved: every non-Qwen family tested, at up to 24B, sat below the task's format-competence floor, so the registered both-underpowered branch fires and the abstract states the scope as an open limitation. Serving-path attestation is unresolved by construction: fingerprinting methods detect change between snapshots but none attests which decode path served a particular past call, and the timing instrument class is ruled out by the item-4 audit. §3's data also comes from a locally-served open-weights ladder at N = 26, not from the alias-addressed runtime and not at §4's cells — a mechanism gap and an instance gap, both real.
arms.verdict: descriptive — stated as open limitations rather than estimated
arms.caveats: The instance gap (that a cliff observed at N = 26 transfers to N = 13/21/31) is supported by the companion paper's finding that the same constructible template family governs proposals across N, but it is an inference, not a replication. A rival reading the paper does not screen — that the anchor is pretraining recall rather than construction — is named, and the contamination screen written for it (arm_canary_contamination_audit.py) is disclosed as defective in all three probes and not run.

arms.label: Arm CC — code-channel probe (program emission, sandboxed execution)
arms.design: Measures the paper's standing asserted-not-measured rationale: does delegating construction to an executed program escape the template family? Same three trap cells (N = 13, 21, 31), n = 15 weak-tier invocations per cell; the bare arm-F stem with exactly two registered line replacements turning the code-free contract into a program contract (standard-library math only, stated in the prompt). Programs run sandboxed (python -I, 10 s timeout, registered AST allowlist); stdout scored by arm-F conventions unchanged. Competing predictions arm-CH style: P-CC1 anchor stays modal at >= 2 of 3 cells vs P-CC2 modal bucket strictly above the anchor; ties count as neither. Registration, frozen prompts, executor and four-bin smoke test committed and pushed (commit 285deca) before the first invocation.
arms.result: P-CC1 HOLDS at 3 of 3 cells — with registered margin disclosure: N = 21 mode heavy (9/13 exact 2.1000000), N = 13 and N = 31 one-sample modal margins (2/12, 3/12). Robust row: no valid program output exceeds the family argmax anywhere (0/37 above rival); exactly one exceeds the anchor — a single N = 13 program computing the family argmax V(3,4) = 1.7761424 exactly. Sharpens arm CH: the chosen argmax the model cannot build by direct emission (30/31 invalid) is reached once in 37 when arithmetic is delegated, and never passed. Taxonomy: 37 valid, 7 geometry-invalid, 1 blocked import (random), 0 timeouts; 45/45 collected. Versus code-free anchor concentration 56–86%, code-channel pooled anchor-rate is 14/37 with all lost mass below the anchor — dispersion, not escape. Scope: math-only programs; the numpy/scipy library channel deployed loops permit remains a further arm. Corpus to 513 invocations.

arms.label: Arm CC2 — code-channel fresh-draw replication (weak tier)
arms.design: Fresh-draw replication of arm CC on byte-identical prompts (hashes cited from arm_cc_prompts.json), registered together with arm CCS at commit 4d7b7c5 AFTER CC's results were known — motivation disclosed in the registration. 3 cells x 15 weak-tier invocations, same sandboxed executor and arm-F scoring, pre-stated verdict map: R1 ceiling (0 above-rival predicted; falsifier at >=2), R2 anchor-modal at >=2 of 3 cells; REPLICATED / PARTIAL / FAILED named in advance.
arms.result: REPLICATED. R1: 0/41 valid outputs above the family argmax — the registered zero-count prediction, exactly. R2: anchor bucket modal at 3/3 cells — and N=31, one-sample-thin in arm CC, arrived at 10/15 valid with margin 8, firming the cell CC could not. Pooled weak-tier waves: 0/78 above the argmax, one exact argmax build. Taxonomy: 41 valid, 3 geometry-invalid, 1 blocked import. Protocol note disclosed: one invocation (N=13 slot 2) used runtime tools against the no-tools wrapper; scored verbatim per the arm-M convention.

arms.label: Arm CCS — Sonnet-tier code-channel probe (ceiling is channel, not tier)
arms.design: Same byte-identical program-emission prompts, Sonnet-tier proposer, 3 cells x 15. Competing registered predictions: P-CCS1 escape-is-capability-gated (>=20% of valid outputs strictly above the family argmax) vs P-CCS2 zero-count ceiling. Registered with CC2 at commit 4d7b7c5 before sampling.
arms.result: P-CCS2 HOLDS: 0/37 valid Sonnet outputs above the family argmax. The programs are qualitatively different search — simulated annealing over hand-rolled LCG PRNGs, Halton multi-restarts, force-directed relaxation — and the tier barely anchors (5/37, consistent with arm S's direct-emission escape), yet its executed math-only search never passes the family ceiling at any cell. The ceiling is a property of the channel, not the tier. Taxonomy: 37 valid, 7 geometry-invalid, 1 timeout (the programme's first). Pooled over all three code-channel arms: 0/115 above the argmax.

arms.label: Arm CN — held-out-N contamination probe (construction vs recall)
arms.design: Bare template at five N absent from every cited sum-of-radii scoreboard and every prior arm (N = 50, 58, 62, 65, 75; three truncation cells, two m=1 extend cells), 15 weak-tier invocations each. Registered at commit 69a1642 before sampling, in response to an external review that rated the unprobed contamination confound blocking. Competing predictions: P-CN1 construction (registered value modal at >=4/5 cells incl. >=2/3 discriminating) vs P-CN2 recall (<=2/5); UNDERPOWERED floor at 5 valid per cell; ties count against.
arms.result: P-CN1 HOLDS. Mode at 4/5 held-out cells, all three discriminating (margins +6 to +13); k*-structure majority at 5/5 (57/63 valid); 0 rival emissions in 39 discriminating validities; 0/63 above the family argmax. The one miss (N=50) is the arm-CH pattern: 10/11 valid are the 7x7 grid plus one filler, 6 of them with the filler pushed into a corner at r~0.0123 (0.017 below V(7,1)). Validity 63/75, no collapse at large N. The closed form describes what the proposer builds where there is nothing to recall; absence of the fitted cells from pretraining text is not established. Corpus 678.
